chunks: Sulaymān ibn Jaʿfar al-Jaʿfarī asked the righteous servant Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar, peace be upon them, about a man who comes to the market and buys a fur garment, not knowing whether it is from a properly slaughtered animal or from one not properly slaughtered: may he perform salat (prayer) in it?

So he said: “Yes, inquiry is not upon you. Indeed, Abū Jaʿfar, peace be upon him, used to say: ‘Indeed, the Khawārij constrained themselves through their ignorance; indeed, the religion is broader than that.’”

key_terms.الدِّينَ: the religion, described here as broad and accommodating
key_terms.السُّوقَ: the market from which the garment is purchased
key_terms.الْخَوَارِجَ: the Khawārij, cited as an example of excessive strictness
key_terms.الْمَسْأَلَةُ: asking or inquiring into the matter
key_terms.ذَكِيَّةٌ: properly slaughtered according to religious law
key_terms.فِرَاءٍ: fur skins used in the garment

ai.seo_question: Can one pray in a fur garment bought from the market if its slaughter-status is unknown?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling that a person may perform salat (prayer) in a fur garment bought from the market even if he does not know whether the animal was properly slaughtered. It teaches that one is not obligated to investigate such matters in this case, and it condemns excessive self-imposed restriction rooted in ignorance.
